page: Amazon Web Services c8gn.2xlarge is a compute-optimized instance powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor and an ARM64-based AWS Graviton Neoverse-V2 processor. This server features 8 dedicated physical cores and 8 vCPUs running at a clock speed of 2.8 GHz, with no hyperthreading. The CPU cache configuration includes 64 KB of L1d cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 36 MB of L3 cache. It is equipped with 16.0 GB of system memory, providing a resource density of 2.0 GB per core. The instance does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, but it provides a baseline network bandwidth of 25 Gbps.

Benchmark results position the c8gn.2xlarge as a solid performer for compute-heavy workloads. In CPU testing, it achieved a stress-ng single-core score of 1707.39 and a multi-core score of 13646.63, both falling within the average range. It demonstrates strong memory performance, with a PassMark memory score of 2866.41 and a cached read-only small block memory bandwidth of 925.02 GB/sec. Single-threaded bzip3 decompression is a notable strength, scoring 14.47 GB/sec, which is in the top 25 percent of tested servers. However, cryptographic performance is a comparative bottleneck, with the PassMark CPU encryption test returning a weak score of 1510.85.

With its 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio and dedicated ARM64 architecture, the c8gn.2xlarge offers a cost-efficient profile for scale-out compute workloads that do not require local NVMe storage. It is well-suited for tasks such as static web serving, where it achieves a throughput of 20.3 GB/sec, and database operations, processing 18.36 million Redis SET operations per second. It also supports lightweight machine learning tasks, handling prompt processing for a small 135M LLM model at 554.05 tokens per second, though performance drops significantly on larger models. This makes the instance ideal for containerized microservices, software compilation, and network-bound utility workloads.
